title: Document Review Findings
description: Return contract for a persona sub-agent. The sub-agent returns this JSON in its final message — there is no artifact file.

reviewer.description: Persona name that produced this output (e.g. 'coherence', 'feasibility', 'product')

findings.description: Review findings. Empty array if none.

title.description: Short, specific title. 10 words or fewer.

severity.description: Critical: a contradiction or gap that will block or derail implementation. Major: a real issue implementers/readers will hit. Minor: a small clarity or completeness gap. Informational: net-new content/scope requests and advisory observations — excluded from the actionable count.

section.description: Document section where the issue appears

why_it_matters.description: Observable consequence first — what a reader/implementer/downstream decision gets wrong, not a restatement of the document text. ~2-4 sentences; cap embedded quotes at ~30 words.

finding_type.description: error: something the document says that is wrong (contradiction, design tension, incorrect statement). omission: something the document forgot to say (missing step, absent detail, undefined threshold, forgotten cross-reference).

autofix_class.description: safe_auto: one clear correct fix (typo, wrong count, stale cross-reference, terminology drift, summary/detail mismatch with body authoritative, mechanically-implied addition). gated_auto: a concrete fix that touches document meaning/scope and warrants confirmation (substantive additions implied by the doc's own decisions, codebase-pattern-resolved fixes, framework-native-API substitutions, missing standard controls, factually-incorrect behavior). manual: requires user judgment; genuinely multiple valid approaches.

suggested_fix.description: Concrete fix text committing to ONE recommendation (single, multi-facet, or composite) — no menu of alternatives. Required for safe_auto and gated_auto; for manual, include only when the fix is obvious. Omit only when there is genuinely no good fix (a bad suggestion is worse than none).

confidence.description: 0: false positive or pre-existing — do not emit. 25: might be real but unverifiable — do not emit. 50: verified but a nitpick or advisory ('nothing breaks, but…') — surfaces as an FYI observation. 75: double-checked, a competent implementer/reader will concretely hit it — actionable. 100: the document text, codebase, or cross-references leave no room for interpretation — actionable.

evidence.description: Quoted text from the document supporting the finding. >=1 item. For anchor 75/100, the first item is the verbatim line that makes the finding true.

residual_risks.description: Risks noticed but not confirmed as findings

deferred_questions.description: Questions to resolve in a later workflow stage

_meta.return_note: The return above IS what the sub-agent sends in its final message. The orchestrator merges from these returns — no run-id, no artifact tree.
_meta.confidence_gate: Governs the actionable tier only. Anchors 0/25: dropped silently. Anchor 50: FYI observation (no decision forced). Anchors 75/100: actionable (enter routing). Net-new/Informational findings and the residual_risks/deferred_questions buckets are non-actionable and surface for awareness regardless of anchor.
_meta.net_new_overlay: A finding requesting content or scope the document never set out to cover is Informational, surfaced for awareness and excluded from the actionable count.
